fy_label_note: Baba/Visible Alpha FY-YYYY = TriNet calendar year (FY-2025 adjusted EBITDA $425M on $5,010M revenue matches the company's reported 8.5%, doc 141105). Window FY2021 to FY2026E. Peer labels: NSP and PAYC calendar years; ADP and PCTY fiscal years end June, PAYX ends May, so those three lead the calendar label by about half a year.

peers.notes: Baba has no PEO industry bucket: TNET sits in Application Software and Insperity in HR services (Baba comps for 'Human resource training and employment services' returned staffing and recruiting names, none closer than NSP). Barrett (BBSI) is not in the Baba universe. ADP and PAYX run large PEOs but are mostly payroll/HCM software; PAYC and PCTY compete for the same SMB HR buyer but carry no insurance risk. The 5-name median is therefore driven by software margins that the health-claims shock cannot touch; NSP is the only risk-bearing PEO comparator and is shown as a sensitivity.

track_record.notes: 10-K FY2025 ICFR language shows no material weakness; no restatement found. Retention fell to about 80% in 2025 with 'pricing cited most often as the reason for leaving TriNet' and co-employed WSEs down 11% (doc 141105): client loss on price, recorded as share loss.

tenure.ceo: Michael Q. Simonds (external hire from Unum; not founder). Predecessor Burton Goldfield ran the company through the FY2022 to FY2023 peak, so the people promising the reversal are not the people who presided over the peak.
tenure.long_tenured: ceo_months >= 84 or founder: NO (31.5 months, not founder)

deciding_facts: Margin fell 554 bps (14.02% FY2022 to 8.48% FY2025) while revenue rose 2.1%, a cost and pricing problem, and management concedes a cohort was 'significantly underpriced'; the 5-name peer median rose 866 bps (ratio -1.56).

Against the only risk-bearing PEO (Insperity, -401 bps) the ratio is 0.72, so the health-claims shock was real and industry-wide, but TriNet still lost 153 bps of its lead over NSP and lost clients on price (retention about 80%).
confidence_note: Rule triggers (negative ratio on the 5-name set, margin down on rising revenue) are robust, but the 5-name median is mostly HCM software with no claims exposure. On a PEO-only lens this reads closer to mixed: a genuine external claims shock amplified by underpricing.
